lines.text: Why is the sky blue? Why not purple, or white?
lines.speaker: buddy

lines.text: Good question. The answer is hiding inside sunlight.
lines.speaker: host

lines.text: Sunlight looks white, but it is really every colour mixed together.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Each colour travels as a wave. Red waves are long. Blue waves are short.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: When sunlight hits the air, tiny gas molecules bounce the short blue waves all over the sky.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Blue light scatters almost six times more than red light.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Violet scatters even more. But the sun sends less violet, and our eyes are less sensitive to it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So the sky is blue because the air scatters blue sunlight in every direction.
lines.speaker: host
